claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline is a single-phase FCC alloy.
The equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
Differences in deformation and failure behavior across the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys are not explained merely by constituent count.
Cr, Mn, and Ni form element-specific nanoclusters at grain boundaries in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi.
Synergistic segregation or mutual interactions among Cr, Mn, and Ni drive grain-boundary nanocluster formation in the quinary alloy.
Grain-boundary nanoclustering of Cr, Mn, and Ni reduces grain-boundary cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi.
Grain-boundary nanoclusters promote crack initiation along grain boundaries during intermediate-temperature deformation of CrMnFeCoNi.
Intermediate-temperature ductility loss in CrMnFeCoNi is correlated with grain-boundary cracking.
Removing one or more key elements disrupts the segregation mechanism responsible for grain-boundary nanoclustering.
Equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets contain fewer or less critical grain-boundary nanoclusters than the quinary alloy.
Reduced grain-boundary nanoclustering in the quaternary and ternary alloys improves grain-boundary cohesion.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have higher ductility under comparable deformation conditions.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will show delayed crack initiation.
The proposed mechanism applies under intermediate-temperature, controlled-strain-rate deformation of thermomechanically processed single-phase FCC alloys.
Holding thermomechanical processing constant while removing constituents provides the controlled compositional comparison.
Atom probe tomography can detect and quantify grain-boundary segregation and nanoclusters in these alloys.
Failure to observe both reduced nanocluster density and a corresponding ductility or crack-initiation shift in the lower-component alloys would falsify the proposed mechanism.
